body:
## Blocks

#40.

## What happens

Every Margin verb fails on a `dtplyr` input whose Grouping plan names a factor
or ordered-factor dimension, whenever `.margin_label` is not `NULL` — which is
the default:

```r
library(marginplyr)
library(dplyr)

df <- data.frame(g = factor(c("lo", "hi")), v = 1:2)
collect(summarize_with_margins(dtplyr::lazy_dt(df), s = sum(v), .grouping = rollup(g)))
#> Error in encode_factor_for_margin(g, missing_sentinel = "..marginplyr_missing_factor_code",  :
#>   could not find function "encode_factor_for_margin"
```

All four verbs, measured against the installed 0.1.0 at `b3190d2`:

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `summarize_with_margins()` | `ERR: could not find function "encode_factor_for_margin"` |
| `expand_with_margins()` | same |
| `nest_with_margins()` | same |
| `nest_by_with_margins()` | same |
| `summarize_with_margins(.margin_label = NULL)` | OK |
| a character dimension instead of a factor | OK |
| the same factor on the local backend | OK |

## What is claimed

`R/summarize_with_margins.R:222` — rendered into `man/summarize_with_margins.Rd`
and inherited by all four verbs:

> Factor and ordered-factor columns are the one exception, on the backends
> whose factors marginplyr can rebuild: local data frames, `dtplyr`, and
> DuckDB. There it decomposes them to insert `.margin_label` and rebuilds them
> itself, so their levels and ordering are preserved

#23's User Story 2 asks for the same thing: "I want Parent shares to work with
double, logical, Date, factor, and character grouping dimensions according to
their documented contracts, so that grouping-key storage type does not change
correctness."

## Cause

Two sites inject an *unqualified* internal symbol as the head of an expression
`dtplyr` defers:

- `R/margin-label.R:437` — `rlang::expr(encode_factor_for_margin(...))`
- `R/factor.R:133` — `rlang::expr(reconstruct_factor_vector(...))`

Neither function is exported. On the local backend dplyr evaluates the
expression where the symbol resolves; `dtplyr` translates it into a
`data.table` call evaluated in the environment the pipeline was **written** in,
where it does not:

```
build=globalenv collect=globalenv -> ERR
build=globalenv collect=namespace -> ERR
build=namespace collect=globalenv -> OK
build=namespace collect=namespace -> OK
```

The comment at `R/factor.R:127-130` explains why every *argument* is injected
as a value rather than named — a source column could shadow the local (#76).
The function head was not given the same treatment.

## Why no gate catches it

`testthat::test_env("marginplyr")` is `env_clone(asNamespace("marginplyr"))`:

```
$ Rscript -e 'e <- testthat::test_env("marginplyr"); cat(environmentName(parent.env(e)), exists("encode_factor_for_margin", envir = e), "\n")'
imports:marginplyr TRUE
```

so every internal symbol resolves in the environment the tests write
`lazy_dt()` in. `tests/testthat/test-margin-label.R:124` ("dtplyr obeys the
eight-case contract as the local backend does") exercises exactly the failing
combination and passes. No Rd example or vignette covers it either:
`retail_sales` carries no factor column, and the only `factor()` near a dtplyr
chunk (`vignettes/get_started.qmd:575`) is on the local path.

This is why the full suite, the `Live dtplyr` release-matrix job, and both
tarball checks are all green on a tree where the call errors for every user.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `summarize_with_margins()`, `expand_with_margins()`, `nest_with_margins()`,
      and `nest_by_with_margins()` all return the documented result for a
      factor and for an ordered-factor dimension on a `dtplyr` input with the
      default `.margin_label`, with levels and ordering preserved.
- [ ] A regression test that **fails without the fix**. A test written in the
      ordinary way cannot: it must build the `lazy_dt()` input and collect it
      in an environment that does not inherit `asNamespace("marginplyr")` —
      e.g. `local(..., envir = new.env(parent = globalenv()))`. State that
      requirement at the test, because the next reader will otherwise simplify
      it back into a passing no-op.
- [ ] Whatever other unqualified internal symbol is injected into a deferred
      expression is found and fixed in the same pass, not only these two. Scan
      for `rlang::expr(` and `rlang::call2(` heads in `R/`.
- [ ] The test obeys `AGENTS.md` *Release matrix*: it may require `dtplyr` and
      no other member of `optional_backends()`.

## How it was found

The Docs & Tests audit of #40's readiness review, against `b3190d2`, and
reproduced independently before filing.
